scenario_text: A finite two-level subsystem is held in equilibrium with a heat bath at temperature T, and the energy separation between its lower and upper levels is Δ. The target is the equilibrium fraction of subsystems occupying the upper level, determined by the relative thermal statistical weights of the two levels. All other environmental properties are treated as fixed background conditions, so no time evolution is required.
baseline_mechanisms: Thermal redistribution between two discrete energy levels.
Equilibrium statistical weighting of accessible microscopic states.
baseline_assumptions: The subsystem is fully equilibrated with a heat bath.
Only two energy levels are accessible.
The two levels have equal, fixed degeneracy.
Interactions between distinct subsystems are negligible.
scientific_constraints: The target fraction must lie in the closed interval from zero to one.
The target must be nondecreasing with temperature.
The target must be nonincreasing with energy separation.
The total population of the two levels is normalized.
refinement_agenda: Change the equal-degeneracy assumption to allow distinct degeneracies for the two levels.
Add additional accessible energy levels and their degeneracies.
Add weak interactions between subsystems that alter the equilibrium level weights.
Change the equilibrium assumption to study finite-time relaxation toward the thermal population.

scenario_text: A disordered electronic solid conducts through thermally activated hopping of localized charge carriers between nearby sites. The benchmark predicts the equilibrium electrical conductivity from temperature and material-specific activation parameters, with phonons providing the fixed thermal background that enables hopping. The baseline excludes field heating, contact effects, and competing conduction channels so that the temperature dependence is governed by a single activation mechanism.
baseline_mechanisms: Thermal activation of localized charge carriers between neighboring sites.
Charge transport through a single effective hopping channel.
baseline_assumptions: The material is spatially homogeneous and isotropic on the scale of the measurement.
A single effective activation energy characterizes all relevant hopping events.
The conductivity prefactor is independent of temperature over the benchmark range.
The applied electric field is weak enough that field heating and field-assisted hopping are negligible.
scientific_constraints: Conductivity must be nonnegative.
Conductivity must increase monotonically with temperature for positive activation energy.
Conductivity must decrease monotonically with activation energy at fixed temperature.
The conductivity prefactor and activation energy must remain positive.
refinement_agenda: Add a distribution of hopping barriers to represent structural disorder more explicitly.
Add a competing extended-state conduction channel at higher temperature.
Allow the hopping process to become field-assisted under strong applied fields.
Change the single-barrier assumption to include temperature-dependent localization or carrier-density effects.

spec.target_description: Equilibrium electrical conductivity of the disordered solid

scenario_text: A population of unstable nuclei is isolated so that its abundance changes only through spontaneous nuclear decay. The benchmark predicts the instantaneous rate of change of the undecayed-nucleus population over a fixed observation interval. The isotope identity and its decay characteristics are held fixed across trajectories, while the initial population varies. Daughter production and external irradiation are excluded from the baseline mechanism.
baseline_mechanisms: Spontaneous conversion of unstable parent nuclei into decay products
Independent decay activity of the parent nuclei with a fixed isotope-specific decay characteristic
baseline_assumptions: The sample is isolated from external particle or photon irradiation.
The parent nuclei are sufficiently dilute that they do not interact with one another.
The decay characteristic is constant throughout the observation interval.
Daughter products do not feed back into the parent population.
scientific_constraints: N must remain non-negative.
N must be non-increasing in time.
The decay rate must vanish when the parent population vanishes.
refinement_agenda: Add coupled daughter-nuclide populations and their subsequent decays.
Change the assumption of isolation by adding an external production or irradiation source.
Add branching channels with distinct decay characteristics.
Change the constant-decay-characteristic assumption to model time-dependent environmental modification of the nuclear state.

domain_mechanisms.description: an energetically allowed reaction or decay channel
scale-dependent coupling or finite-size response
interaction between physically distinct amplitudes

spec.target_description: Instantaneous time derivative of the population of undecayed radioactive nuclei
expected_behaviors: The undecayed population decreases monotonically with time.
The population remains non-negative for all simulated times.
The magnitude of the decay rate is proportional to the remaining undecayed population.
The trajectory approaches zero asymptotically rather than becoming negative or reaching zero at a finite generic time.
forbidden_behaviors: Population growth without an external source
Dependence on daughter abundance, irradiation intensity, or environmental transport in the baseline model

scenario_text: A small mass attached to an ideal spring is displaced and released, while a surrounding medium provides weak velocity-dependent resistance. The mass position and velocity evolve in time under the restoring interaction and dissipative resistance, with no external drive. The benchmark targets the instantaneous rate of change of velocity along trajectories initialized with varied positions and velocities. The expected motion is oscillatory with gradually decreasing amplitude.
baseline_mechanisms: Elastic restoring interaction proportional to displacement.
baseline_assumptions: The mass moves along one fixed spatial axis.
The spring remains within its linear elastic regime.
The resistance is instantaneous and depends only on the current velocity.
Mass, elastic stiffness, and resistance parameters remain constant during each trajectory.
scientific_constraints: Mass and elastic stiffness are positive.
The resistance coefficient is nonnegative.
Mechanical energy cannot increase in the unforced baseline system.
The equilibrium displacement is fixed at zero.
refinement_agenda: Add a nonlinear elastic restoring contribution for large displacement.
Add a nonlinear resistance mechanism at higher speeds.
Change the assumption of no external forcing by introducing a time-dependent drive.
Change the fixed-parameter assumption to model slowly varying stiffness or resistance.

domain_mechanisms.description: velocity-dependent nonlinear dissipation
nonlinear or spatially varying restoring/drive force
temperature-dependent or regime-dependent friction
force mediated by an already modeled auxiliary state

spec.target_description: Instantaneous acceleration of the mass along the damped spring trajectory.

required_dynamic_states.description: Displacement of the mass from the spring's equilibrium position.

scenario_text: An isolated stationary source produces a radially directed electric field in vacuum, and the benchmark measures the field magnitude at a selected observation point. The source strength and the distance from the source are independently varied between trials. The baseline model captures radial spreading of the field without time dependence, material polarization, or nearby conductors. The target is the instantaneous electric-field magnitude at the observation point.
baseline_mechanisms: Radial spreading of a stationary electric field from a localized source.
baseline_assumptions: The source is pointlike relative to the observation distance.
The surrounding space is homogeneous, isotropic, and unbounded vacuum.
The source charge is stationary during each measurement.
The reported target is field magnitude rather than vector direction.
scientific_constraints: q is strictly positive.
r is strictly positive.
E is nonnegative.
At fixed q, E decreases with r; at fixed r, E increases with q.
refinement_agenda: Add finite source size or spatial charge distribution as a change in the point-source assumption.
Add dielectric polarization or spatially varying material response as an additional field mechanism.
Add nearby conducting boundaries and induced charges as a boundary-condition refinement.
Extend the model to time-varying sources so that retardation and radiation become dynamic mechanisms.

scenario_text: A particle with fixed kinetic energy encounters a one-dimensional rectangular barrier whose width and energy excess above the particle are independently varied. The benchmark predicts the stationary transmission probability produced by quantum tunneling through the barrier. The baseline model treats the particle as a coherent wave and assumes the barrier is isolated, static, and lossless.
baseline_mechanisms: coherent wave propagation in the classically forbidden region
quantum tunneling through a finite one-dimensional barrier
wave matching at the two barrier interfaces
baseline_assumptions: The barrier is rectangular, static, and spatially isolated.
The incident particle has a sharply defined energy and a single mass.
The evolution is one-dimensional and coherent.
The barrier does not absorb or decohere the particle.
scientific_constraints: The transmission probability is bounded from zero to one.
Barrier width, barrier energy excess, and particle mass are strictly positive.
The particle energy lies below the barrier energy by construction.
refinement_agenda: Add a second barrier to introduce coherent multiple-reflection interference.
Change the rectangular-barrier assumption to a smoothly varying barrier profile.
Add a finite incident energy bandwidth and predict an energy-averaged transmission.
Change the lossless assumption to include an explicitly quantum absorptive region.

scenario_text: A Newtonian liquid is driven steadily through a straight circular tube, and the pressure decrease between two axial locations is measured. The baseline response is produced by viscous momentum transport across the tube radius under fully developed, unidirectional flow. Experiments independently vary the volumetric flow rate, dynamic viscosity, tube length, and tube radius while remaining in the smooth-flow regime. The task is to recover the static dependence of the pressure drop on these quantities.
baseline_mechanisms: Radial viscous transport of axial momentum.
Balance between the imposed axial pressure gradient and internal viscous resistance.
baseline_assumptions: The liquid is incompressible and Newtonian with spatially uniform viscosity.
The flow is steady, axisymmetric, and fully developed over the sampled length.
The tube is straight, rigid, circular, and hydraulically smooth.
Inertial disturbances, entrance effects, and wall slip are negligible.
scientific_constraints: Pressure drop must be nonnegative for nonnegative flow in the chosen downstream direction.
The response must be monotonic increasing in flow rate, viscosity, and tube length.
The response must be monotonic decreasing in tube radius.
The baseline relation must be dimensionally consistent for pressure.
refinement_agenda: Add entrance and exit losses when the sampled section is not fully developed.
Release the smooth-flow assumption and introduce wall roughness effects.
Allow transition to an inertia-dominated or turbulent resistance regime.
Allow non-Newtonian shear-dependent viscosity or finite wall slip.
Introduce density variation if compressibility becomes significant.

spec.target_description: Pressure drop along the sampled length of the tube, measured in pascals.

input_symbols.description: Volumetric flow rate through the tube in cubic meters per second.
Dynamic viscosity of the liquid in pascal-seconds.

expected_behaviors: The pressure drop increases proportionally with flow rate when the other inputs are fixed.
The pressure drop increases proportionally with dynamic viscosity and sampled tube length.
Increasing the tube radius causes a strong monotonic decrease in pressure drop.
The response approaches zero as the imposed flow rate or sampled length approaches zero.
forbidden_behaviors: Negative pressure drop for a positive flow rate under the stated orientation.
An increase in pressure drop when tube radius increases while all other inputs remain fixed.
Finite nonzero pressure drop at zero flow rate in the baseline model.
Oscillations, discontinuities, or multiple response branches within the stated regime.
